title: Chicken, breast, meat and skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Boneless chicken breast is a lean source of protein, and in this case the skin is included, making the product richer in calories and fat. Raw chicken breast is used for marinating, pâtés, and in some traditional dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken meat is the most widely consumed meat worldwide.
Chicken breast contains less fat than other parts of the bird, but the skin adds a significant amount of fat and calories.
Raw chicken can carry Salmonella, so it must be handled and cooked carefully.
In some cuisines, such as Japanese, raw chicken breast is used in dishes like tartare after special marination.
Chicken bones left after trimming are rich in calcium and are often used to make broth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides about 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Raw chicken breast contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It is a good source of niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, essential for bones, immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The high protein content helps maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw chicken may harbor Salmonella and Campylobacter; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High fat in skin
items.content: Chicken skin is high in saturated fat, which may be undesirable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Antibiotic residues
items.content: Some farmed birds are given antibiotics; choose products labeled ‘antibiotic‑free’ when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw chicken is rarely eaten plain. It is often marinated in acidic liquids (lemon juice, vinegar) and used in dishes like tartare, sushi rolls, or as a filling for stuffed vegetables after thorough preparation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw chicken breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for 1‑2 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
